A reflow oven takes about **45 minutes of heat-up** and is switched on **35–60 minutes before its SMT line starts**, so the heat-up is finished when the first board arrives.

A WARNING is raised at **1,125 kW** (projected 15-minute demand ≥ 90% of the 1,250 kW contract), or when the forecast probability of exceeding the contract in the next hour is ≥ 20%. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-04_glossary.md#EM-04 Glossary > Billing and demand terms > Warning line]

Why that level: 1,125 kW is 90% of the 1,250 kW contract capacity, so it is a buffer that flags the supervisor early enough to shed load and bring projected demand back under contract before the 15-minute interval ends. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Purpose]

Demand above the contract capacity is billed at a **premium rate on the excess kW**, not on the whole interval demand:

- The excess is billed at **2× the period's contract price** for the portion up to **10% over the contract** (i.e. up to 1,375 kW).
- The portion **beyond 10% over** (above 1,375 kW) is billed at **3× the period's contract price**.

Contract capacity is 1,250 kW on a regular contract, so the 10% threshold is 125 kW over (1,375 kW total). [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-03_tariff_guide.md#EM-03 Tariff Guide > Exceedance charges]

This is separate from the normal monthly demand charge, which is a flat per-kW charge on the contracted capacity regardless of use. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-04_glossary.md#EM-04 Glossary > Billing and demand terms > Demand charge]

The night-load baseline uses a CUSUM with **k = 0.5** (allowance) and **h = 8 robust sigmas** (alarm threshold), firing when it crosses that limit and the night load is more than 3 kW above expectation.

The load forecaster predicts the **change** from an anchor rather than the demand level because of a limitation of tree models:

- Tree models (LightGBM) cannot predict a value above anything they saw in training, and the plant rarely exceeded its contract in the training data. A level model therefore tends *not* to warn about an exceedance — the first version with a level target actually missed the exceedances.
- Predicting a change lets the model add a heat-driven or start-up-driven increment on top of the current load.

The anchor is:
- short horizons (15 min to 3 h): the last completed interval
- day-ahead: the same time last week

[source: docs/forecasting.md#Load forecasting > Model]

I have the full procedure. Here's what operators should do.

**Before the peak (pre-cool and stage):**
- Pre-cool the building/areas earlier in the day so thermal load is front-loaded, avoiding new cooling load in the peak window [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Purpose].
- Confirm the EV-01 pause function works and warn staff that charging may be paused [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Procedure > Step 4: EV pause readiness].
- Do not load both burn-in rooms (BI-01, BI-02) in the same quarter hour; delay the next loading if demand is high [source: docs/knowledge/equipment/EQ-03_burn_in_room.md#EQ-03 Burn-in Room Manual > Start-up sequence > Loading discipline].

**When the forecast/WARNING signals possible exceedance of the 1,250 kW contract:**
1. Pause EV-01 charging immediately — removes up to 100% of EV load (28 kW) without touching production [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Procedure > Step 4: EV pause readiness].
2. Delay the next burn-in loading on BI-01/BI-02 [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook].
3. Raise the chilled-water setpoint +1 °C (≈4% of present chiller load) if the pre-cooling margin allows [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Procedure > Step 6: during the peak].
4. Lower compressed-air setpoint 0.5 bar on AC-01/AC-02/AC-03 [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook].
5. Monitor projected demand every interval; if WARNING/ALARM is raised, follow SOP-03 and shed in playbook order [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-06_heat_wave_precooling.md#SOP-06 Heat Wave Pre-cooling > Procedure > Step 6: during the peak].

**Ordering and limits:**
- The playbook puts the least disruptive actions first; EV charging is shed first because it has no production impact [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook].
- Never shed: server room (DC-01), running molders (IM-01–IM-04), or reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01–RF-03) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed].
- Exceedance is billed at 2× the contract price up to 10% over, and 3× beyond that [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-04_glossary.md#EM-04 Glossary > Billing and demand terms > Exceedance].

**Cause:** 10 machines (805 kW rated) started simultaneously within 3 minutes at ~07:57 — SMT lines, reflow ovens (RF-01/02/03), injection molders (IM-01/02/03/04), chiller CH-02, wave solder (WS-01), and air compressor AC-02 [data: list_detections]. This is the "Monday morning simultaneous start" scenario S2.

**15-minute stagger effect:** Re-simulation drops the peak from 1,324.4 kW to 1,141.5 kW (−182.9 kW), eliminating the exceedance and avoiding up to NT$6,652 (US$208) in penalties [data: whatif_staggered_start].

Yes. A compressed-air leak was detected in September 2025.

**Detection:** BASELINE layer, event AIR_LEAK, detected 2025-09-09, covering the night-load rise from 2025-09-03 (meters AC-01, AC-02, AC-03), severity medium. Size ≈ **18.1 kW** above the usual night baseline, running around the clock, costing about NT$652,462/year. [data: list_detections]

**Inspection procedure (SOP-04):**
1. Confirm the signal — check night load of AC-01/02/03, confirm meters are reporting (SOP-07), and rule out night production (e.g. IM-03/IM-04). [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-04_compressed_air_leak.md#SOP-04 Compressed Air Leak > Procedure > Step 1: confirm the signal]
2. Choose the time — do the ultrasonic walk-down in a quiet period, ideally at night or on a Sunday. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-04_compressed_air_leak.md#SOP-04 Compressed Air Leak > Procedure > Step 2: choose the time for the walk-down]
3. (Roles: Energy coordinator reviews the alert; Facilities engineer leads the walk-down and repair; Shift supervisor releases the area.) [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-04_compressed_air_leak.md#SOP-04 Compressed Air Leak > Roles]
4. Tag — tag each leak with a numbered tag, record location/type/estimated size (small/medium/large), photograph where practical. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-04_compressed_air_leak.md#SOP-04 Compressed Air Leak > Procedure > Step 4: tag]
5. Repair — isolate/depressurize, replace the faulty fitting/hose/valve, re-pressurize and recheck with the detector, remove the tag and record closure. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-04_compressed_air_leak.md#SOP-04 Compressed Air Leak > Procedure > Step 5: repair]
6. Verify — watch compressor night load for several nights; target is return to the earlier baseline; if it doesn't return, repeat the walk-down. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-04_compressed_air_leak.md#SOP-04 Compressed Air Leak > Procedure > Step 6: verify]

Note: the detection is a night-load-baseline alert (medium severity), not a confirmed single leak location — the walk-down is needed to find and size individual leaks.

RF-02 used **1,976.9 kWh** (energy cost NT$6,045, energy charge only) from Friday 12:00 to Monday 12:00 on 17-20 October 2025 [data: get_energy].

The weekend shutdown procedure (SOP-02) says:
- **Purpose:** switch off non-essential loads at week's end to prevent idle weekend energy, whose largest single source is a reflow oven left in standby [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Purpose].
- **Verification after shutdown:** each shut-down machine should read OFF (≤3% of rating); no reflow oven may be IDLE or RUNNING; and the plant base load should be ~500 kW — a figure well above that indicates something was left on [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Verification].

RF-02's 1,976.9 kWh over the weekend is consistent with a reflow oven that was not fully shut down, which is what triggered the flag.

Here's what happened to MDB-3.

**What happened:** The MDB-3 capacitor bank tripped out of service on 3 November 2025 (incident S8), and the board's power factor fell from ~0.96 to ~0.84, where it stayed through 12–13 November. The hourly series confirms the drop: ~0.96 before 3 Nov, then a flat ~0.85 plateau from 4 Nov onward.

**Daytime PF on 5 November (08:00–17:00):** mean 0.849, range 0.845–0.852 [data: get_meter_series]. That is below the 0.90 rule threshold but above the 0.80 surcharge line.

**Maintenance should check (per SOP-05):** the MDB-3 capacitor bank for an out-of-service condition — a tripped breaker, blown fuse, failed contactor, or failed capacitor. Procedure: verify the bank is out of service and record PF before/after, days out of service, and the fault found; then isolate the bank, replace the failed fuse/contactor/capacitor, and re-energize. If the failure repeats, keep the bank out of service and call the electrical contractor for a full inspection [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-05_power_factor_check.md#SOP-05 Power Factor Check > Procedure > Step 3: restore].

Note: MDB-3 is sensitive to its capacitor bank, and the injection molders' base PF is ~0.86 (dropping ~0.12 at no load), so a low-load board can read lower — SOP-05 requires load above 10% of rating to avoid a false low-PF reading [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-05_power_factor_check.md#SOP-05 Power Factor Check > Expected PF values].
